stem: While comparing federal and state law, a pharmacist compares Syndros oral solution with Marinol capsules. Select all rules that apply to Syndros.

choices.text: Under these facts, a Schedule II prescription for Syndros may not be refilled for dronabinol oral solution.
In this setting, the Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period applies for dronabinol oral solution.
Given the described event, syndros follows the Schedule III refill rule used for Marinol for dronabinol oral solution.
On this record, its liquid dosage form makes it Schedule VI for dronabinol oral solution.
At this stage, syndros is Schedule II even though dronabinol capsules marketed as Marinol are Schedule III for dronabinol oral solution.

related_facts: dronabinol oral solution (Syndros) is used for chemotherapy-associated nausea and vomiting and aids-related anorexia; it is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II.
Federal law prohibits refilling a Schedule II prescription; additional dispensing requires a new lawful prescription or a permitted remainder of a partial fill.
A Massachusetts written or electronic Schedule II prescription becomes invalid 30 days after its issue date.
